topic: Kids in kimono at the shrine
title_jp: {七五三|しちごさん}と{千歳飴|ちとせあめ}
context: Sunday 15 November, the day of 七五三. On a morning walk to {鷹ノ原神社|たかのはらじんじゃ}, アルちゃん finds children in kimono everywhere and asks the {田中|たなか} family LINE group what's going on. Today: polite thanks and congratulations.
scene: Sunday morning at the town shrine: kids in kimono everywhere. You ask the {田中|たなか} family group chat what's going on.

phrases.jp: {ご丁寧に|ごていねいに|kindly, so thoughtfully|3}、ありがとうございます。
phrases.en: That's very kind of you, thank you.
phrases.note: For a small gift or extra kindness: warmer than a plain ありがとうございます. The classic reply to a thank-you present.

phrases.jp: {七五三|しちごさん|Shichi-Go-San (kids' shrine day)|3}、おめでとうございます。
phrases.note: Say it to the parents (or the child) you meet at the shrine. With strangers, congratulations always stay polite.

phrases.jp: {写真|しゃしん}、{お撮り|おとり|(humble) taking (a photo)|2}しましょうか？
phrases.note: Humble お + stem + しましょうか offers to do something for someone. You'll hear back: いいんですか？お{願|ねが}いします！

phrases.jp: そんな、{気を遣わないで|きをつかわないで|to be considerate, go to trouble|4}ください。
phrases.note: When someone hands you a thank-you gift. Say it once, then accept with ありがとうございます.

phrases.jp: なるほど、それで{混んでる|こんでる|to be crowded|4}わけですね。
phrases.en: I see, so that's why it's so crowded.
phrases.note: それで…わけですね = 'so that's why…': a polite way to show a new fact made something click.

dialogue_setting: The {田中|たなか} family LINE group, Sunday morning: アルちゃん is at {鷹ノ原神社|たかのはらじんじゃ}; {恵子|けいこ}さん and {颯太|そうた} are at home.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {神社|じんじゃ|Shinto shrine|4}に{着物|きもの|kimono|3}の{子|こ}がいっぱいいる！{何|なに}かの{お祭り|おまつり|festival|4}？
dialogue.en: There are loads of kids in kimono at the shrine! Is it some festival?

dialogue.speaker: 颯太
dialogue.jp: {七五三|しちごさん|Shichi-Go-San (kids' shrine day)|3}だよ！{俺|おれ}も5{歳|さい}の{時|とき}{行った|いった}
dialogue.en: It's 七五三! I went too when I was five.

dialogue.speaker: 恵子さん
dialogue.jp: 3{歳|さい}・5{歳|さい}・7{歳|さい}の{子|こ}の{成長|せいちょう|growth|3}を、{神社|じんじゃ|Shinto shrine|4}で{お祝い|おいわい|celebration|3}するのよ
dialogue.en: We celebrate how 3-, 5- and 7-year-olds are growing up, at the shrine.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: だからみんな{写真|しゃしん}を{撮ってる|とってる}わけだ！{細長い|ほそながい|long and thin|3}{袋|ふくろ}も{持ってる|もってる}
dialogue.en: So that's why everyone's taking photos! They're carrying long thin bags too.

dialogue.speaker: 颯太
dialogue.jp: それ、{千歳飴|ちとせあめ|'thousand-year' candy|2}！{俺|おれ}は{袴|はかま|hakama (formal pleated trousers)|2}がイヤで{泣いた|ないた}らしい
dialogue.en: That's {千歳飴|ちとせあめ}! Apparently I cried because I hated my hakama.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: あ！{居間|いま|living room|3}の{写真|しゃしん}の{子|こ}、それで{泣いてた|ないてた}わけだ！
dialogue.en: Oh! So that's why the kid in the living-room photo is crying!

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: さっき{家族|かぞく}の{写真|しゃしん}を{撮って|とって}あげたら、{千歳飴|ちとせあめ|'thousand-year' candy|2}をくれた
dialogue.en: Just now I took a family's photo for them, and they gave me {千歳飴|ちとせあめ}.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: でも『ありがとう』しか{言えなかった|いえなかった}…{失礼|しつれい|rude|4}だったかな？
dialogue.en: But all I could say was 'thanks'… Was that rude?

dialogue.speaker: 恵子さん
dialogue.jp: {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}よ！{次|つぎ}は『{ご丁寧に|ごていねいに|kindly, so thoughtfully|3}ありがとうございます』って{言えば|いえば}{完璧|かんぺき|perfect|3}よ
dialogue.en: It's fine! Next time say 'that's very kind of you, thank you' and it'll be perfect.

listening.intro: As you leave the shrine, {颯太|そうた} sends a voice message.

lines.jp: アルちゃん、{早く|はやく}{戻って|もどって}きて！{千歳飴|ちとせあめ|'thousand-year' candy|2}、{半分|はんぶん}ちょうだい！
lines.en: アルちゃん, come back quick! Give me half the candy!

grammar.form: verb / い-adj: plain form + わけだ ({撮|と}ってる → {撮|と}ってるわけだ, {寒|さむ}い → {寒|さむ}いわけだ) · な-adj: + な + わけだ ({静|しず}か → {静|しず}かなわけだ) · noun: + な + わけだ ({休|やす}み → {休|やす}みなわけだ) · polite: わけです ({混|こ}んでるわけですね)
grammar.explanation: Say it when a fact you've just learned explains something you'd already noticed: 'so that's why', 'no wonder'. It often follows だから or それで. Don't mix it up with わけではない (the next point), which denies a conclusion: 'that doesn't mean…'.

examples.jp: {窓|まど}が{開いてる|あいてる}。{寒いわけだ|さむいわけだ}。
examples.en: The window's open. No wonder it's cold.

examples.jp: {明日|あした}は{祝日|しゅくじつ|public holiday|3}か。{電車|でんしゃ}が{混んでる|こんでる|to be crowded|4}わけだ。
examples.en: Tomorrow's a holiday? So that's why the train is packed.

examples.jp: {健太|けんた}は{大阪|おおさか}{出身|しゅっしん|coming from (hometown)|3}なんだ。それで{関西弁|かんさいべん|Kansai dialect|3}なわけだ。
examples.en: {健太|けんた} is from Osaka. So that's why he speaks Kansai-ben.

quiz.question: {雪|ゆき}が{降って|ふって}る。{寒い|さむい}＿＿。
quiz.en: It's snowing. No wonder it's cold.
quiz.explain: The snow explains the cold, so わけだ. わけではない = 'it doesn't mean', わけがない = 'there's no way', ことにした = 'decided to'.

quiz_more.question: {今日|きょう}は{田中|たなか}さんの{誕生日|たんじょうび}なんだ。それでケーキがある＿＿。
quiz_more.en: It's 田中さん's birthday today. So that's why there's a cake.
quiz_more.explain: A new fact (the birthday) explains what you see (the cake): わけだ. The others talk about plans or timing.

quiz_more.question: スペインの{人|ひと}なんだ。{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}＿＿わけだ。
quiz_more.en: He's from Spain? No wonder he's a good cook.
quiz_more.explain: A な-adjective keeps な before わけだ: {上手|じょうず}なわけだ. {上手|じょうず}だわけだ is wrong.

kanji.where: Printed in red and gold on the long paper bags children carry at {七五三|しちごさん}, often with cranes and turtles, symbols of a long life.
kanji.breakdown: {千歳飴|ちとせあめ}: 千 thousand + 歳 years (of age) + 飴 candy → 'thousand-year candy', a wish for a long life.
kanji.related: {鶴|つる} = crane, {亀|かめ} = turtle: both drawn on the bag for long life.

tip.title: Why 3, 5 and 7?
tip.body: Odd numbers count as lucky, so children visit the shrine at 3, 5 and 7 (traditionally boys at 5, girls at 3 and 7). The official day is 15 November, but most families go on any weekend in October or November, often with a studio photo shoot. {千歳飴|ちとせあめ} is pulled long to wish the child a long life.

challenge.prompt: {恵子|けいこ}さん: 「お{昼|ひる}は{お赤飯|おせきはん|red-bean rice for celebrations|2}よ。{早く|はやく}{帰って|かえって}きてね」 You can't wait. Which sticker do you send?
challenge.hint: How do you say 'can't wait' to family?
challenge.explanation: {楽|たの}しみ！ = 'can't wait!', the natural warm reply to family. {承知|しょうち}しました is office keigo, far too stiff for your host mum; ガーン is for bad news, and なんでやねん is a Kansai comeback for something absurd.

vocab.note: Look for the {鳥居|とりい} gate. A Buddhist temple is お{寺|てら}.
着 wear + 物 thing. At {七五三|しちごさん} boys often wear {袴|はかま} instead.
{成長|せいちょう}する = to grow up. Used for children, plants, even companies.
お{祝|いわ}いする = to celebrate. Also the money or present itself.
{居|い} be, stay + {間|ま} room. Common in family homes; リビング is the modern word.
{失礼|しつれい}します = excuse me, entering or leaving a room.
ご{丁寧|ていねい}に = 'how kind of you'. {丁寧語|ていねいご} is the です/ます style.
Very common in speech: {完璧|かんぺき}！ = nailed it.

vocab.en: to be considerate; to go to trouble for others
vocab.note: Often written {気|き}を{使|つか}う. {気|き}を{遣|つか}わないで = don't go to any trouble.
{混|こ}んでる = crowded right now. Opposite: {空|す}いてる (empty).

kanji_study.parts: 礻 the altar radical (things for the gods) + 兄, here a kneeling person with an open mouth → someone saying a blessing at the altar: celebrate.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 視 (look): 祝 has 兄 on the right, 視 has 見.

kanji_study.parts: 戸 a door + 大 a big person → someone coming back in through the door: return.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 房 (room; tassel): 戻 has 大 under 戸, 房 has 方.

extras.intro: Words you'll see and hear at any shrine.

items.note: Bow lightly before you pass under it.

items.jp: お{参り|まいり|visit to pray|4}
items.en: a visit to a shrine or temple

items.note: 5{円|えん} is popular: ご{縁|えん} means a good connection.
Tie a bad one to the rack and leave it behind.
For exams, traffic safety, love, health…

extras.title: Polite words for gifts and celebrations
extras.title_jp: お{祝|いわ}いとお{礼|れい}の{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: Set phrases for giving, receiving and congratulating.

items.jp: ご{結婚|けっこん|marriage|4}おめでとうございます
{つまらない||boring, trifling|3}ものですが…
items.en: It's nothing much, but… (giving a gift)
items.note: Modest, a bit old-fashioned; ほんの{気持|きも}ちです is softer.

items.jp: お{気持ち|きもち}だけで{十分|じゅうぶん}です
ありがとうございます。いただきます
items.en: Thank you, I'll gladly take it.

items.note: Given back for a celebration present, usually half its value.
